```{r}
# Load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(tmap)
library(sf)
library(spData)
library(knitr)
```

## Historically red-lined neighborhoods in LA

```{r}
#1. Create a map of historically red-lined neighborhoods, colored by HOLC grade
# Load data
la_map <- st_read('data/mapping-inequality/mapping-inequality-los-angeles.json')
la_ej <- st_read('data/ejscreen/EJSCREEN_2023_BG_StatePct_with_AS_CNMI_GU_VI.gdb') |> filter(CNTY_NAME == 'Los Angeles County')
crashes <- st_read('data/SWITRS_LA/Crashes.csv')

#Map red-lined areas in LA County
tm_basemap("OpenStreetMap") +
tm_shape(la_map) +
    tm_polygons(fill = 'grade',
        fill.scale = tm_scale(values = c('darkgreen', 'deepskyblue2', 'darkgoldenrod1', 'brown2')), 
       fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "HOLC Ranking")) +
tm_scalebar(position = tm_pos_in("right", "top")) +
tm_compass(position = tm_pos_in('right', 'bottom')) +
tm_legend(position = tm_pos_out('right', 'center')) +
tm_layout(
    main.title = 'Historical Redlining in Los Angeles County (HOLC ranking)'
)
```


```{r}
# Summary table of % census block groups within and outide of each HOLC grade

# Join holc data and ej data
# Check if coordinate reference systems match
if(st_crs(la_map) == st_crs(la_ej)){
  print('File coordinate reference systems match')
} else{
  warning('File coordinate reference systems do not match.  Transform one file before joining')
}
la_map <- st_make_valid(la_map)

# Transform la_ej to match la_mpa
ej_transformed <- st_transform(la_ej, crs = st_crs(la_map))

# Confirm transformation
if(st_crs(la_map) == st_crs(la_ej)){
  print('File coordinate reference systems match')
} else{
  warning('File coordinate reference systems do not match.  Transform one file before joining')
}

# Check whether census blocks overlap
if (any(st_intersects(la_map, ej_transformed, sparse = FALSE))){
  print('census blocks overlap')
} else {
  print("census blocks do not overlap")
}

#Convert to planar data
sf_use_s2(FALSE)

# Join files
holc_ej <- st_join(y = la_map, x = ej_transformed,  join = st_within, left = TRUE) |> st_drop_geometry()

#Confirm join success
if (nrow(holc_ej) == nrow(ej_transformed)){
  print('Join was successful: all census blocks included')
} else {
  print("join failed.")
  print(paste('holc_ej has', nrow(holc_ej), 'rows'))
  print(paste('ej_transformed has ',nrow(ej_transformed), 'rows'))
}

# 2. Create a table summarizing:
### percent of census blocks sithin each HOLC grade
### percent of cencus blocks that don't fall within a census grade

# Create the summarization table
holc_ej |> group_by(grade) |> summarize(
    Percent = ((n()/nrow(holc_ej))*100)
) |> knitr::kable(col.names = c("HOLC Grade", "Percent of Census Blocks"))


```
## Current Conditions by HOLC Ranking


```{r}
# Plot percent Low Income by HOLC Ranking
holc_ej |> group_by(grade) |> drop_na(LOWINCPCT)|> summarize(low_inc_pct = mean(LOWINCPCT)) |> ggplot(
    mapping  = aes(x = grade, y = low_inc_pct, fill = grade)) + 
    geom_bar(stat = 'identity') +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c('darkgreen', 'deepskyblue2', 'darkgoldenrod1', 'brown2', 'lightgray'), name = 'HOLC Ranking') +
    xlab("HOLC Ranking") +
    ylab("Percent Low Income Population") +
    ggtitle("Mean Proportion of Low-Income Residents by HOLC Ranking") +
    theme_minimal()

# Plot percentile for PM2.5 by HOLC Ranking
holc_ej |> group_by(grade) |> drop_na(P_PM25)|> summarize(pm25_percentile = mean(P_PM25, drop_na = TRUE)) |> ggplot(
    mapping  = aes(x = grade, y = pm25_percentile, fill = grade)) + 
    geom_bar(stat = 'identity') +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c('darkgreen', 'deepskyblue2', 'darkgoldenrod1', 'brown2', 'lightgray'), name = 'HOLC Ranking') +
        xlab("HOLC Ranking") +
    ylab("Percentile") +
    ggtitle("Mean National Percentile Ranking for Exposure to Fine Inhalable \nAir Pollutants (PM2.5) by HOLC Ranking") +
    theme_minimal()

# Plot percentile for Low Life Expectancy by HOLC Ranking
holc_ej |> group_by(grade) |> drop_na(P_LIFEEXPPCT)|> summarize(lowlifeexp_percentile = mean(P_LIFEEXPPCT)) |> ggplot(
    mapping  = aes(x = grade, y = lowlifeexp_percentile, fill = grade)) + 
    geom_bar(stat = 'identity') +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c('darkgreen', 'deepskyblue2', 'darkgoldenrod1', 'brown2', 'lightgray'), name = 'HOLC Ranking') +
    xlab("HOLC Ranking") +
    ylab("Percentile") +
    ggtitle("Mean National Percentile Ranking for Low Life Expectancy by HOLC Ranking") +
    theme_minimal()
```

On average, areas that received an HOLC ranking of C and D currently have a greater proportion of people with low incomes, greater exposure to air pollutants, and have a lower life expectancy. 30% of census blocks in Los Angeles county are located in areas that received a ranking of C or D. Those census blocks have a disporptionately higher population of low-income residents, at just over 40% of their population. They rank over the 80th national percentile in exposure to fine inhabalble air particles and just under the 60th percentile for low life expectancy; they experience more air pollution of fine particles than 80% of census blocks across the US and lower life expectancy than 60%. In contrast, in areas that recieved a ranking of A (just over 1% of LA county's census blocks), less that 20% of the population is low-income.  Areas that recieved an A still rank in the 60th percentile for fine air particle exposure, but just over the 20th percentile for life-expectancy.  This indicates that the New Deal HOLC ranking system has resulted in measurable demographic differences decades later.  Past diversion of investments from areas with low rankings likely contributes to current disparities in wealth and environmental safety as redlined areas received less real estate investment and resulting social, safety, and  environmental investment.  Lower wealth and greater environmental health risks likely combine with other socioeconmic factors to create the observed disparity in life expectancy. 

## Part 2: Legacy of redlining in pedstrian and bike accidents

```{r}
#Check NAs in Lattitude/Longitude vs Point_X/Point_Y
crashes |> filter(crashes['LONGITUDE'] == "NA") |> dim()
# Missing data for 97350 rows
crashes |> filter(crashes['POINT_X'] == "NA") |> dim()
# Missing data for 9484 rows
crashes_points <- crashes |> select(-c('LATITUDE', 'LONGITUDE'))

#Conver crash points to geometry class
crashes_spatial <- crashes_points |> mutate(
    POINT_X_numeric = as.numeric(POINT_X),
    POINT_Y_numeric = as.numeric(POINT_Y)
    )|> drop_na(
        POINT_Y_numeric, POINT_X_numeric
    ) |> st_as_sf(
        coords = c('POINT_X_numeric', 'POINT_Y_numeric'),
        crs = 4326) # Set crs to WGS 84

#Check that CRS match
if(st_crs(crashes_spatial) == st_crs(la_map)){
  print('File coordinate reference systems match')
} else{
  warning('File coordinate reference systems do not match.  Transform one file before joining')
}

# Transform crs of crashes points to match joined holc_ej
crashes_transformed <- st_transform(crashes_spatial, crs = st_crs(la_map))

#Confirm CRS change
if(st_crs(crashes_spatial) == st_crs(la_map)){
  print('File coordinate reference systems match')
} else{
  warning('File coordinate reference systems do not match.  Transform one file before joining')
}

#Join with HOLC data
crashes_holc <- st_join(y = la_map, x = crashes_transformed,  join = st_intersects, left = TRUE) |> st_drop_geometry()

#Confirm join success
if (nrow(crashes_holc) == nrow(crashes_transformed)){
  print('Join was successful: all crashes included')
} else {
  print("join failed.")
  print(paste('crashes_holc has', nrow(crashes_holc), 'rows'))
  print(paste('crashes_transformed has ',nrow(crashes_transformed), 'rows'))
}

#Summarize bike/pedestrain crash trends by HOLC grade and plot by HOLC Ranking
crashes_bike_ped <- crashes_holc |> filter(BICYCLE_ACCIDENT == "Y" |
    PEDESTRIAN_ACCIDENT == "Y") |> drop_na(grade)
crashes_bike_ped |> group_by(grade
    ) |> summarize(percent = n()/nrow(crashes_bike_ped) *100
    ) |> ggplot(
      mapping  = aes(x = grade, y = percent, fill = grade)) + 
    geom_bar(stat = 'identity') +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c('darkgreen', 'deepskyblue2', 'darkgoldenrod1', 'brown2', 'lightgray'),
      name = "HOLC Ranking") +
    xlab("HOLC Ranking") +
    ylab("Percent of Crashes") +
    ggtitle("Percentage of bicycle and pedestrian \ncrashes in LA County by location HOLC ranking") +
    theme_minimal()
```

Pedestrian and cyclist safety appears to follow similar patterns with HOLC ranking as income and air pollution, likely contributing to the disparity in life expectancy. Among areas that received an HOLC ranking, less than 5% of crashes occur in areas with a ranking of A, but over 60% occur in areas wth rankings of C and nearly 30% in areas ranked as D. This likely resulted from less investment in safety infrastucture and maintenance in these historically lower-income areas, especially if hazard reporting, funding, and county response times are influenced by income and demographic factors. To strategically improve pedestrian and cyclist safety, the County of LA can invest in more safety measures in historically redlined areas and critically examine how it makes decisions related to safety infrastructure investment and maintenance.
